subject: Split-path latency — proposed SLA credit for 2027-02-09 incident
messages:
From: Paul Geller <paul.geller@nodechain.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: High tail latency across write path (02/09) — request for credit

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

We observed elevated p99/p999 latency and a growth in 5xxs for our write-heavy traffic to your hosted inference pool between 15:07–15:38 UTC on 2027-02-09. That spike impacted production traffic and caused backpressure in our ingestion pipeline.

Attached is a small sample export from our side (latency-sample-nodechain-20270209.csv) showing the request timestamps and end-to-end duration. NodeChain is asking for a credit as the incident exceeded our SLA threshold.

Notes:
- We saw a clear step-up at 15:12 UTC where p999 moved from ~420ms to ~2.1s for routed requests to eu-west model variants.
- Our origin recorded retries that matched increased token generation latency from your API.

Please confirm whether this window is eligible for credit or excluded due to your maintenance event that you flagged in the status page (maintenance-id: MNT-2114). If you consider it a partial degradation rather than a maintenance exclusion, we would expect a proportional credit.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Geller
Head of Platform Reliability, NodeChain

On Tue, Feb 9, 2027 at 4:28 PM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Paul — I received the sample ...

Quick technical summary from infra:
- We rolled a router patch in MNT-2114 (15:05–15:10 UTC) which should have been non-disruptive for active connections; the control plane change briefly increased routing table recomputes.
- Observed telemetry: routing table recompute spikes at 15:06 UTC, followed by elevated queue depth on the write shard (shard-wr-07) from 15:07–15:34 UTC.
- Error profile: ~62% of the elevated latency samples in NodeChain’s CSV are within 15:07–15:20 UTC and show a retry loop at the client layer. The remaining samples (15:21–15:34) map to gradual recovery correlated with autoscaler spin-up.

Interpretation and recommendation:
- This appears to be a split-path event: a brief maintenance-triggered control-plane disturbance (excluded) that cascaded into a partial degradation of the write serving layer (not excluded). The partial degradation prolonged the impact well past the maintenance window.
- Proposed credit: a proportional credit based on the percentage of affected requests outside of the maintenance window. Per our analysis, ~70% of the latency/exceptions you saw were outside the 15:05–15:10 UTC excluded window. I recommend we offer 70% of a daily uptime credit for the affected service-class (write-api) for 2027-02-09.

Attachment: ingest_kpis-20270209.log (engineer sampling)

Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: High tail latency across write path (02/09) — request for credit

Stephanie / Marcus — thanks for the quick analysis. Marcus, good call on the split-path framing.

From the billing side, we typically compute credits as: (service-class daily uptime credit) × (proportion of requests affected outside maintenance). For NodeChain’s GA write tier the daily credit cap is 100% of one day’s usage for severe incidents, pro-rated otherwise.

If we go with Marcus’s 70% figure:
- Proposed customer-facing credit: 70% of one day’s write-tier invoice for 2027-02-09, applied as a billing credit and separate line item.
- Next steps: Stephanie, please confirm with legal if we need a formal sign-off (DocuSign) for the credit amount; otherwise billing will schedule the adjustment for the next invoice cycle and we'll send a credit memo.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High tail latency across write path (02/09) — proposed credit and next steps

Paul — thanks again for the report and the sample. We investigated and reproduced the timeline: an operational change rolled during MNT-2114 (15:05–15:10 UTC) triggered a routing recompute that cascaded into a partial degradation on shard-wr-07. That degradation extended to 15:34 UTC while autoscaling brought capacity back online.

Proposal (summary):
- Rationale: 30% of affected traffic falls within the maintenance exclusion window (15:05–15:10 UTC). The remaining ~70% occurred outside that excluded window and is therefore eligible for a proportional credit.
- Credit: 70% of one day’s write-tier invoice value for 2027-02-09, applied as a billing credit. We will issue a credit memo on the next invoice cycle; if you prefer immediate settlement we can route a one-time invoice adjustment (DocuSign not required for a billing credit under $50k).
- Evidence: we attached engineered telemetry (ingest_kpis-20270209.log) and your sample — happy to share anonymized service-side traces on request.

If this is acceptable, please reply with ACCEPT and we’ll confirm the memo and timing. If you want a formal credit agreement, we can send a DocuSign and route through legal (ETA 2–3 business days).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Ops Liaison, Redwood Inference
